KeenZ😶‍🌫️: 感谢大家对上一条推文的关注

https://x.com/0xkeenz/status/2031114389215223813

KeenZ
感谢大家对上一条推文的关注！🫡

没想到这么多人被 Qwen 3.5 的预填充（Prefill）问题困扰。今天熬夜翻了些资料，发现事情比想象中更复杂：

1️⃣ 关于 LM Studio 的 MLX 引擎

其实是单一统一架构：所有 mlx 模型都走 mlx-lm 的文本核心，视觉能力只是可选的模块化挂载（纯文本输入时完全不加载视觉部分）。我之前的判断过于“简单粗暴”了（自罚一杯 🥃）。

官方详细介绍：https://lmstudio.ai/blog/unified-mlx-engine…

2️⃣ Qwen 3.5 为什么反复预填充？

这是一个复合问题：mlx_lm KV Cache 失效 + Qwen 官方 Jinja 模板解析问题 + 模型本身架构特性 三者共同导致的。这种底层冲突导致每次对话都会触发全量预填充，目前社区还没完美的“一键修复”方案。

具体讨论看 GitHub Issue：https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/issues/903…

目前 Mac 跑本地 OpenClaw，优先选 @karminski3
推荐的 GLM 4.7 Flash。大家跑 Qwen 3.5 还有遇到类似的玄学问题吗？评论区蹲几个大佬聊聊！🙌

#LMStudio #OpenClaw #AppleSilicon #Qwen #MLX
@0xkeenz

终于破案了！感谢牙医大佬指路 🫡 之前用 Qwen 3.5 35B A3B 和 27B 跑 OpenClaw 总碰到 Prompt 反复载入问题，慢到怀疑人生。原以为是配置问题，结果竟是 mlx_vlm 的锅 🤡 今天换到 GLM 4.7 Flash (走 mlx_lm)，响应直接从几分钟缩短到 5-20 秒！本地 OpenClaw 终于能丝滑跑起来了，Apple Silicon x.com/karminski3/sta…

Caching doesn't seem to be working for Qwen3.5 · Issue #903 · ml-explore/mlx-lm

https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/issues/903

dexloom opened this issue on 2/17/2026

Running lm_server with Qwen3.5 is completely different in terms of caching, it always processes whole prompt, cached tokens counter in response is always 0.

awni commented on 2/17/2026

The mamba cache cannot be trimmed to so there are fewer cases where you get a cache. Basically if you are continuing a conversation caching should work. But if you using the same system prompt with a new query it will have to reprocess the system prompt.

Could you say more about your use case?

kernelpool commented on 2/17/2026

I was running into the same issue (when using a coding agent) so I hacked together something quick as a workaround - maybe something like kernelpool@8e08dbb could work?

dexloom commented on 2/17/2026

Could you say more about your use case?

Local MLX server running Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B MXFP4, custom agent, supporting jinja templates, I am pretty sure beginning of the conversation including system prompt remains the same, switching back to Minimax I have no problems. I've checked server logs to confirm as well.

mzbac commented on 2/17/2026

The mamba cache cannot be trimmed to so there are fewer cases where you get a cache. Basically if you are continuing a conversation caching should work. But if you using the same system prompt with a new query it will have to reprocess the system prompt.

Could you say more about your use case?

@awni I was checking the cache today, noticed people with dual RTX 6000 pro can handle 190k context window with 4bit minimax m2.5 but I keep getting OOM on my m2 192GB, so far I think the prompt cache for thinking model may have some issues, I can see the the LRU keeps inserting cache entries for multi turn conversation for the same session, so far my findings:

for thinking models, the key also contains reasoning tokens that the client typically does not replay (because reasoning isn’t used when tokenizing the next request https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/main/mlx_lm/server.py#L163) .

In that case the sequences diverge much earlier:

  • cached key: P + R + A + EOS
  • next prompt: P + A + …

Shared prefix is basically just P, so the cache can only reuse up to the end of the previous prompt and you still re-prefill a lot of tokens. It’s not always a total miss (it’s a longer hit + trim), but it’s a bad hit for speeding up multi-turn.

I am not very familiar with the prompt cache implementation, but from the symptoms, it looks like when there is a longer cache hit and it is trimmed, a new cache entry is inserted into the LRU.

awni commented on 2/17/2026

Hmm, that sounds like a plausible issue. Will take a look.

angeloskath commented on 2/18/2026

So the lru prompt cache leaves the cache in memory when trimming. That was meant as an optimization since you can fork conversations for free.

However it is obviously problematic when the cache is 10GB and then you copy it 10x so you spend 100GB on a cache...

I think the fix is fairly simple, the cache needs to be aware of how much cache size is currently being used and how much is available. If we are reaching the limit it should evict instead of copying etc.

For the Mamba cache the fix is going to be a bit more involved. I haven't checked what other frameworks do in that case but I don't see how we can get around the fact that we can't remove things from a mamba cache. So the only solution is to preemptively cache it.

awni commented on 2/18/2026

There is also this adversarial case with reasoning that might merit a specific solution:

If you have something like this:

Request 1: [System] [User A]
Response 1: [Reasoning] [Assistant A]
Request 2: [System] [User A] [Assistant A] [User B]

Then the prompt cache won't match exactly since the second request drops the reasoning tokens. This is actually the right behavior for most models, but it's adversarial for the LRU prompt cache. Since we will copy the cache and keep the old copy which includes the reasoning tokens that is never used again.

awni commented on 2/18/2026

I think maybe the right thing to do is for a reasoning model only save the prompt cache to just prior the reasoning output.

So in the above example the prompt cache would be [System] [User A] instead of [System] [User A] [Reasoning] [Assistant A]

This would also help with hybrid models since we would have the cache at a usable point.

dexloom commented on 2/23/2026

Made something that could work for caching Qwen3.5, #923

spicyneuron commented on 3/4/2026

Could we split prompt caching into two tracks?

For non-trimmable caches (ArraysCache / SSM state), store sparse snapshots only for those layers, then keep regular KV cache as a single rolling state. On reuse, restore the latest SSM anchor before the prefix and trim the regular cache to that position.

This would give partial-cache recovery without full checkpoints, with lower memory overhead and / or more granular restore points.

EDIT: Could be an enhancement after #911

angeloskath commented on 3/5/2026

@spicyneuron that is pretty much the plan. Put more generally, apply the logic per layer rather than per model.

skymen commented on 3/6/2026

Any idea when this will be fixed/improved?

I am using opencode + lm studio to run Qwen3.5 35B-A3B MLX 4bit quantized and while token generation is really really fast, it reprocesses the whole prompt on every message and on every tool call, so something that would take 10-15 seconds ends up taking 1m46s and the waiting times get exponentially worse the fuller the context.

I've had a prompt on a bigger project run for 45mn before I interrupted it.

SlimG commented on 3/8/2026

I have the same issue with mlx-lm 0.31.0 and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-4bit, using OpenCode 1.2.13 as client.
I am not a proficient programmer, but I've done my due diligence with troubleshooting this issue, and I find it difficult to wait, so I had Claude (Opus 4.6) analyze the problem to make me a temporary fix that seem to work for me during testing. I'm sharing it here for any other impatient soul who can't wait to get their hands on Qwen3.5 😉

Claude's analysis of why the checkpoint mechanism in PR #911 doesn't help Qwen3.5:

The checkpoint cache is stored with a key that includes the last user message content. When the client sends request #2, it modifies earlier messages (e.g. removing tags), so the checkpoint key diverges from the new prompt. The server finds a "longer match" but can_trim_prompt_cache() returns False because ArraysCache.is_trimmable() inherits False from _BaseCache. Result: fetch_nearest_cache returns None, tokens — full cache miss.

Claude's workaround:

For hybrid models, move the checkpoint from just before to just before the last user message. This way the checkpoint key becomes [System + Tools] — a stable prefix that matches across requests without needing to trim ArraysCache.

My test results (identical setup, two-message conversation):

Before patch After patch
Qwen3.5 request #2 11962/11967 tokens processed (full miss) 57/379 tokens processed (cache hit)
GLM-5 request #2 320/321 (unaffected) 320/321 (unaffected)
MiniMax-M2.1 request #2 348/351 (unaffected) 348/351 (unaffected)

Patch (replace _compute_prompt_checkpoint in server.py):

def _compute_prompt_checkpoint(self, tokenizer, request, prompt):
    if request.request_type != "chat":
        return False, -1
    if request.messages[-1]["role"] != "user":
        return False, -1
    try:
        test_cache = make_prompt_cache(self.model_provider.model)
        is_hybrid = not can_trim_prompt_cache(test_cache)
    except Exception:
        is_hybrid = False
    if is_hybrid:
        im_start_id = None
        try:
            im_start_id = tokenizer._tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(
                "<|im_start|>"
            )
        except Exception:
            pass
        if im_start_id is not None:
            im_start_count = 0
            for i in range(len(prompt) - 1, 0, -1):
                if prompt[i] == im_start_id:
                    im_start_count += 1
                    if im_start_count == 2:
                        checkpoint_offset = len(prompt) - i
                        return True, -checkpoint_offset
    prompt_checkpoint = -1
    if tokenizer.has_thinking:
        for i in range(1, min(11, len(prompt)) - 1, 1):
            if prompt[-i] == tokenizer.think_start_id:
                prompt_checkpoint = -i - 1
                break
    return True, prompt_checkpoint

Known limitations:

  • single checkpoint per request,
  • hardcoded <|im_start|> (ChatML only),
  • _serve_single codepath not covered.

Looking forward to the proper solution. This is a vibe-coded workaround that may very well introduce it's own issues. Ye have been warned 😉

spicyneuron commented on 3/9/2026

For me, 0.31.0 fixed <think> but revealed another cache breaker: tools rendering.

Using Claude Code 2.1.71 with Qwen 3.5's chat template, tools render differently after the first turn. Example diff between the turn 1 and 2 requests:

@@ -85,9 +90,6 @@
           "description": "- Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size\n- Supports glob patterns like \"**\/*.js\" or \"src
\/**\/*.ts\"\n- Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time\n- Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns\n- When you a
re doing an open ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Agent tool instead\n- You can call multiple tools
in a single response. It is always better to speculatively perform multiple searches in parallel if they are potentially useful.",
           "parameters": {
             "$schema": "https:\/\/json-schema.org\/draft\/2020-12\/schema",
-            "additionalProperties": false,
-            "type": "object",
-            "required": ["pattern"],
             "properties": {
               "pattern": {
                 "description": "The glob pattern to match files against",
@@ -97,7 +99,10 @@
                 "description": "The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter \"undefined\" or \"null\" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.",
                 "type": "string"
               }
-            }
+            },
+            "type": "object",
+            "required": ["pattern"],
+            "additionalProperties": false
           },
           "name": "Glob"
         },

The chat template's tojson preserves these differences at the beginning of each chat, so the cache always misses.

I verified that recursively sorting tools before passing to the chat template fixes the issue, but this arguably shouldn't be a default behavior because:

  • This is mostly a client bug, even though the server can fix it.
  • This might render keys in a different order than models were exposed to during training. Probably doesn't matter, but hard to know without testing.
  • Should we sort tools array order or just the JSON object keys? Both could cause the cache miss.

EDIT: Easiest fix is just adding sort_keys to Qwen 3.5's chat template:

@@ -47,7 +47,7 @@
     {{- "# Tools\n\nYou have access to the following functions:\n\n<tools>" }}
     {%- for tool in tools %}
         {{- "\n" }}
-        {{- tool | tojson }}
+        {{- tool | tojson(sort_keys=True) }}
     {%- endfor %}
     {{- "\n</tools>" }}
     {{- '\n\nIf you choose to call a function ONLY reply in the following format with NO suffix:\n\n<tool_call>\n<function=example_function_name>\n<parameter=example_parameter_1>\nvalue_1\n</parameter>\n<parameter=example_parameter_2>\nThis is the value for the second parameter\nthat can span\nmultiple lines\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>\n\n<IMPORTANT>\nReminder:\n- Function calls MUST follow the specified format: an inner <function=...></function> block must be nested within <tool_call></tool_call> XML tags\n- Required parameters MUST be specified\n- You may provide optional reasoning for your function call in natural language BEFORE the function call, but NOT after\n- If there is no function call available, answer the question like normal with your current knowledge and do not tell the user about function calls\n</IMPORTANT>' }}
@@ -117,9 +117,9 @@
                     {{- '\n<tool_call>\n<function=' + tool_call.name + '>\n' }}
                 {%- endif %}
                 {%- if tool_call.arguments is defined %}
-                    {%- for args_name, args_value in tool_call.arguments|items %}
+                    {%- for args_name, args_value in tool_call.arguments|dictsort %}
                         {{- '<parameter=' + args_name + '>\n' }}
-                        {%- set args_value = args_value | tojson | safe if args_value is mapping or (args_value is sequence and args_value is not string) else args_value | string %}
+                        {%- set args_value = args_value | tojson(sort_keys=True) | safe if args_value is mapping or (args_value is sequence and args_value is not string) else args_value | string %}
                         {{- args_value }}
                         {{- '\n</parameter>\n' }}
                     {%- endfor %}

EDIT 2: Chat template alone doesn't reliably fix. Tool args can also shift, at least with Claude Code:

             "id": "8fa12cc6-b035-46fe-b265-d4fa0bb43e0a",
             "function": {
               "name": "Grep",
-              "arguments": "{\"pattern\":\"function\\\\s+\\\\w+\",\"output_mode\":\"content\",\"head_limit\":10,\"type\":\"js\"}"
+              "arguments": "{\"pattern\":\"function\\\\s+\\\\w+\",\"head_limit\":10,\"output_mode\":\"content\",\"type\":\"js\"}"
             },

And this one isn't quite so easy to patch in the template.

EDIT 3: Here's a cache-friendlier Qwen 3.5 chat template: https://huggingface.co/spicyneuron/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MLX-4.8-bit/blob/main/chat_template.jinja

This will still always need to redo the last turn because of the model's SSM layers, but it's much faster than processing from the beginning, and is likely the best that's possible without diverging from the official chat template.

To sum up, there are multiple things that line up to make Qwen 3.5 difficult to cache:

  1. Untrimmable SSM layers (fixed in 0.31.0)
  2. Floating <think> tags (fixable via something like what @SlimG proposed, but only causes reprocessing the previous turn)
  3. Unsorted tools / args (fixable via chat template)

Entirely possible there's something else too... but 1 + 3 is working well for me so far.

Claude's analysis of why the checkpoint mechanism in PR #911 doesn't help Qwen3.5: The checkpoint cache is stored with a key that includes the last user message content. When the client sends request #2, it modifies earlier messages (e.g. removing tags), so the checkpoint key diverges from the new prompt. The server finds a "longer match" but can_trim_prompt_cache() returns False because ArraysCache.is_trimmable() inherits False from _BaseCache. Result: fetch_nearest_cache returns None, tokens — full cache miss. Claude's workaround: For hybrid models, move the checkpoint from just before to just before the last user message. This way the checkpoint key becomes [System + Tools] — a stable prefix that matches across requests without needing to trim ArraysCache. def _compute_prompt_checkpoint(self, tokenizer, request, prompt): if request.request_type != "chat": return False, -1 if request.messages[-1]["role"] != "user": return False, -1 try: test_cache = make_prompt_cache(self.model_provider.model) is_hybrid = not can_trim_prompt_cache(test_cache) except Exception: is_hybrid = False if is_hybrid: im_start_id = None try: im_start_id = tokenizer._tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids( "<|im_start|>" ) except Exception: pass if im_start_id is not None: im_start_count = 0 for i in range(len(prompt) - 1, 0, -1): if prompt[i] == im_start_id: im_start_count += 1 if im_start_count == 2: checkpoint_offset = len(prompt) - i return True, -checkpoint_offset prompt_checkpoint = -1 if tokenizer.has_thinking: for i in range(1, min(11, len(prompt)) - 1, 1): if prompt[-i] == tokenizer.think_start_id: prompt_checkpoint = -i - 1 break return True, prompt_checkpoint

The chat template's tojson preserves these differences at the beginning of each chat, so the cache always misses.
I verified that recursively sorting tools before passing to the chat template fixes the issue, but this arguably shouldn't be a default behavior because: This is mostly a client bug, even though the server can fix it.
This might render keys in a different order than models were exposed to during training. Probably doesn't matter, but hard to know without testing.
Should we sort tools array order or just the JSON object keys? Both could cause the cache miss. EDIT: Easiest fix is just adding sort_keys to Qwen 3.5's chat template:

To sum up, there are multiple things that line up to make Qwen 3.5 difficult to cache: Untrimmable SSM layers (fixed in 0.31.0)
Floating <think> tags (fixable via something like what @SlimG proposed, but only causes reprocessing the previous turn)
Unsorted tools / args (fixable via chat template) Entirely possible there's something else too... but 1 + 3 is working well for me so far.
